newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold steadfast in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold steadfast in narrow range.

text.p: Gold in Hong Kong remained steadfast in its trading range on Wednesday, with local dealers nodding towards Wall Street as the only incentive for sales.

"People are waiting for some special news out of the U.S. and are looking at the stock market and the forex market, otherwise there is no incentive to sell," a dealer with an international house in Hong Kong said.
"The Dow has already moved over 6,000 but there is still some cash around. If it can move over 6,000 and above, people will sell gold and put their money in equities," he said.
Strong performances on Wall Street in the past week have seen the Dow Jones Industrial Average breach the 6,000 level in intraday trade.
Profit-taking on Monday, as well as caution ahead of the corporate earnings rush saw the Dow lose an overall 13 to 5,967, after an early rally stalled at 6,010.37.
U.S. September producer prices and retails sales data are due to be released on Friday.
Gold in Hong traded across a weak 30 U.S. cent range to end at US$380.80/381.30, just below New York's US$381.10/60 close on Tuesday and unchanged from Hong Kong's previous finish.
"There's uncertainty over where the price will go next, so range-trading is to be expected," a local dealer said.
Another dealing source said that without selling pressure, Hong Kong prices would remain between $380 and $383 an ounce, with strong support at the lower end of the scale.
"There is plenty of support there and people will buy on the dips," he said.
"The downside has support at US$378 and upside resistance is seen at US$382 levels," he said.
Local gold ended HK$1 lower at HK$3,510 a tael.
